title: 1958 AHSME Problem 32
statement: With \(\$1000\) a rancher is to buy steers at \(\$25\) each and cows at \(\$26\) each. If the number of steers \(s\) and the number of cows \(c\) are both positive integers, then:

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: there are two solutions with \(s\) exceeding \(c\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: there are two solutions with \(c\) exceeding \(s\)

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: there is one solution with \(s\) exceeding \(c\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
there is one solution with \(c\) exceeding
\(s\)

solutions.text:
The purchase equation is \[ 25s+26c=1000. \] Reducing modulo \(25\) gives \(c\equiv0\pmod{25}.\) Since \(c\) is positive and \(26c<1000,\) the only possibility is \(c=25.\) Then \[ s=\frac{1000-26(25)}{25}=14. \] There is one solution, and \(c>s.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: The congruence and positivity leave only one possible positive value of \(c\)
